svg.aria-label: Where the licence line falls for an unlicensed person answering an insurance agency's phone, as described in Oklahoma Bulletin 2013-09 and a Tennessee bulletin on unlicensed agency personnel. On the clerical side, an unlicensed person may schedule appointments with a licensed producer, receive requests for coverage to pass to a licensed producer, take factual information about a claim, take factual information for an application, and tell an insured what their policy records show. On the licensed side, only a licensed producer may discuss or explain coverages, advise which coverage to buy, indicate that coverage is or will be bound, bind coverage or sign binders, or answer a request for advice. The script's rule: when a caller asks for advice, the answer is a callback from a licensed producer.
svg.text: Where the licence line falls on the phone
What state regulators say an unlicensed person may and may not do. Any answering-service agent is on the left side.

g.text: Schedule an appointment with a licensed agent
Take a request for coverage, to pass on
Take factual details of a claim
Take factual details for an application
Say what the policy records show

svg.text: Read-only and factual. No opinion on whether it is enough.

g.text: Discuss or explain coverages and terms
Advise which coverage, limit or deductible
Say coverage is, or will be, bound
Bind coverage or sign a binder

svg.text: “You're covered from today” is the sentence to fear.
If a caller asks what they should do, the answer is: “A licensed agent will call you back.” Never an opinion, never a confirmation of cover.
Adapted from Oklahoma Insurance Department Bulletin 2013-09 and Tennessee's bulletin on unlicensed agency personnel. Rules vary by state. Illustration by AI Receptionist Now.
